construct: Thin basement membrane nephropathy is a type IV collagen disorder commonly associated with heterozygous COL4A3 or COL4A4 variants. The classic phenotype is persistent or intermittent microscopic hematuria with relatively preserved kidney function and a diffusely, uniformly thinned glomerular basement membrane. This morphology contrasts with the irregular thickening, thinning, splitting and lamellation classically associated with established Alport nephropathy.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Familial isolated microscopic hematuria with preserved function and no extrarenal features suggests a thin-GBM phenotype; the classic discriminator is diffuse uniform GBM thinning rather than Alport-type irregular splitting/lamellation.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Irregular splitting and lamellation is the closest competitor because it is another type-IV-collagen ultrastructural abnormality, but it supports established Alport nephropathy rather than uniform thin-basement-membrane morphology.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The repaired lead asks for the biopsy discriminator, making diffuse uniform thinning uniquely correct despite modern overlap in collagen-IV nomenclature.
